think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: An elderly female presents with chronic, progressively worsening left ankle pain and subtalar joint destruction without trauma, other joint involvement, constitutional symptoms (fever, weight loss, night sweats), or abnormal inflammatory/arthritic blood markers. The presentation mimics primary seronegative osteoarthritis, masking an indolent musculoskeletal tuberculous infection that only declared itself as persistent non-union and osteolysis following arthrodesis.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Admission triage terminates after the initial presentation, physical examination, normal laboratory/arthritic profile, and plain radiographs/Broden views demonstrating subtalar arthritis, immediately prior to the primary open subtalar joint arthrodesis.
3. Differential Distinctions: Seronegative osteoarthritis and degenerative joint disease cause mechanical pain, osteophytes, and joint space narrowing without systemic inflammatory signs, but achieve solid fusion following arthrodesis. Pyogenic septic arthritis typically presents with acute severe pain, erythema, warmth, fever, leukocytosis, and marked ESR/CRP elevation. Tuberculous arthritis of the foot/ankle (Phemister's triad) is notoriously indolent, presenting with periarticular osteoporosis, peripherally located osseous erosions, gradual joint space narrowing, and a cold abscess or granulation tissue devoid of acute purulence.
case_prompt: A 66-year-old female presents with an 8-month history of progressively worsening pain in the left ankle and inability to stand or walk, particularly over uneven surfaces. She has no history of trauma, joint pain elsewhere, or constitutional symptoms such as fever or weight loss. On physical examination, there is diffuse, tender horseshoe-shaped swelling all around the left subtalar joint with markedly restricted, painful subtalar joint movements. Plain radiographs and 20° and 40° Broden views reveal reduction of subtalar joint space with generalized osteoporosis, confirming subtalar arthritis. Routine blood investigations, including complete blood count and an arthritic profile, are all within normal ranges.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Seronegative Subtalar Joint Arthritis / Primary Osteoarthritis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered the primary diagnosis at presentation given the chronic 8-month history of localized subtalar joint destruction, complete absence of constitutional symptoms, and normal hematological and arthritic panels; however, subsequent surgical non-union, persistent erosions, and histopathology established an infectious tuberculous etiology.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: All blood investigations including arthritic profile were within normal range. She was diagnosed as a case of seronegative type of subtalar joint arthritis.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Pyogenic Bacterial Septic Arthritis / Low-Grade Hardware Infection
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered when the patient exhibited persistent postoperative pain, non-union, and elevated inflammatory markers (CRP 16 mm/L, ESR 36 mm/h, leukocytosis 12,000); however, an intensive four-week course of broad-spectrum intravenous and oral antibiotics produced no clinical improvement, and revision surgery found no purulence.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A course of intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics (1.5 grams of cefoperazone andsulbactam twice a day plus 750 mg of amikacin once a day) was given for 3 weeks followed by 1 week of oral a ntibiotics (linezolid 600 mg twice a day) presuming a presence of low-grade infection.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Revision surgery and debridement revealed dirty granulation tissue without pus, and histopathological analysis demonstrated epithelioid granulomas with abundant Langhans giant cells, establishing the diagnosis of skeletal tuberculosis and resulting in complete bony fusion upon initiation of antitubercular therapy.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Histopathologic examination showed epithelioid granulomas with plenty of giant cells suggestive of tuberculosis (Fig. 7a and b).

editor_comments: Admission breakpoint cleanly placed prior to first surgery. Zero pathogen spoilers. Diagnostic reasoning traces initial misdiagnosis as seronegative arthritis and subsequent rule-out of pyogenic infection with exact verbatim text quotes.
